summary:
This attempt fixed O-034 as a class and O-035 in the doc. Nothing else in the design was rebuilt.

**O-034 (trailing backslash).** One helper, Format-AppArgument in tests/window/WindowCases.ps1, now quotes a path and doubles any trailing backslash run, using eng/read-window.ps1's rule. Invoke-HookedRun and every other case launch now go through it: 12 sites in WindowCases.ps1 and 3 in HookCases.ps1. HookCases.ps1 also loads the helper by name.

The class is listed in tests/window/AppArgumentCorpus.json: 10 roots, 8 plant lines that the hand-quoting pattern must catch or pass, and a census of every script that names or launches the app. The new AppArgumentTests run every row of it through the script's own Invoke-HookedRun and split the result by Windows' own rules. With hand-quoting put back, rows A01–A07 (C:\, D:\, temp\, a spaced folder\, \\127.0.0.1\share\, \\?\C:\, and two trailing backslashes) fail; A08–A10 pass. C-013 now also launches a temp root ending in a backslash through the hook in rows mode, and W-001 ran with `-Root C:\Windows\Logs\`: it wrote its report and held.

**O-035.** docs/design/SL-089-seams.md now says N-006 fails on a row for s only under the kill or timeout ending. Under release, such a row is the positive control (Q-177).

**State I found.** The tree built cleanly before any edit. The four uncommitted .taad/slices/SL-089 records are the engine's own, and I left them untouched.

files.why: Added Format-AppArgument (quote, double a trailing backslash run). Invoke-HookedRun and every Start-App/Invoke-App call given a command line now use it. C-013 adds a rows-mode hooked run of a root ending in a backslash and is now in $HookedCases.
Loads Format-AppArgument by name, which Invoke-HookedRun now calls. Its three Start-App launches use it.
SplitArguments: CommandLineToArgvW, to split a command line the way the app's argv receives it.

Runs the corpus: every root through the script's real Invoke-HookedRun, split and compared with [root, --report, report]; the hand-quoted column checked on every run; the census pattern against its plants; every script that launches the app listed and quoting by the rule.
The O-034 class, enumerated: roots by producer, launch-line plants (fire/quiet), and a census of every script that launches the app.
O-035: says what N-006 fails on, per ending. Also documents that the person's W-001 -Root C:\ command is now safe, and how that is proved.

obligations.how:
I closed the whole class "root ending in a backslash handed to argv undoubled" at the source. Format-AppArgument quotes the path and doubles any trailing backslash run (eng/read-window.ps1:52's rule). Every case launch in WindowCases.ps1 and HookCases.ps1 that builds a command line goes through it, starting with Invoke-HookedRun, which W-001 uses. The corpus at tests/window/AppArgumentCorpus.json holds:
- 10 roots: C:\, D:\, temp\, a spaced folder\, a UNC share\, \\?\C:\, two trailing backslashes, C:, a plain temp root, and a spaced folder with no trailing backslash.
- 8 plant lines.
- A census of 6 scripts.

AppArgumentTests runs all of it. Two more checks fail the build: any script that names or launches the app but is missing from the census, and any hand-quoted launch line in WindowCases.ps1 or HookCases.ps1.

With hand-quoting put back into Invoke-HookedRun, the test fails exactly A01–A07. For example, C:\ reached the app as one argument, `C:" --report <file>`, and two trailing backslashes lost one. A08–A10 still pass.

End to end:
- C-013 launches temp\ through Invoke-HookedRun in rows mode: exit 0, report written, root as passed, dump written. Passed.
- W-001 -Root C:\Windows\Logs\ passed: 1 row, verdict held.

I reworded docs/design/SL-089-seams.md. N-006 fails if a later Windows returns an error for s under the kill or the timeout ending. Under the release ending, a row for s becomes the positive control, and s's absence after Stop is then reported as held beside it (Q-177). This matches Test-N006, which checks for no s row only when the ending is not release.

Q-177's platform-limit branch applies and is recorded in docs/design/SL-089-seams.md. The obligation is owed to validate-slice; nothing in this attempt touches it.

mandatory.where: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Test-N005 (SMB) and Test-N006 (cloud, three endings, Q-177), with -Control. Both passed in earlier attempts. Their launches now go through Format-AppArgument.

tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Test-T009 (held folder drawn 'in use by another program') and N-005's b row ('only partly read: network or share error'). Engine level: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests HeldFolderReasonTests.

tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Test-W001, with W001OracleTests and the W001OracleCorpus. This attempt fixes the defect that stopped `-Root C:\` writing any report (O-034, AppArgumentTests, C-013). The whole-C:\ run is the owner's, per review M8, using the command in docs/design/SL-089-seams.md.
tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Test-R002 steps (f) at 300 characters and (g) at 1000 characters. Both reveal from a panel row and check the landing by leaf Name through Shell.Application.

N-005, N-006 and R-002 ran unattended in earlier attempts, each asserting nothing was left behind. Per review M8, W-001 does not run over C:\ unattended: here it ran on C:\Windows\Logs\ (kernel pool +2 MB).

Test-N006 runs all three controls (release, kill, timeout) and reports 'held: platform gives no failed read (Q-177)'. docs/design/SL-089-seams.md records the platform limit and the silent undercount. This attempt also corrects the wording of what the case fails on (O-035).

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 build FsAnalyser.slnx -c Debug -v q -nologo
tests.note: Run before any edit: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
17/17, including the 3 new AppArgumentTests. WindowCases.ps1 still parses under 5.1 and pwsh and is still ASCII.

tests.command: (mutation) Invoke-HookedRun reverted to hand-quoting, then eng/dotnet.ps1 test --no-build --filter FullyQualifiedName~FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.AppArgumentTests
tests.note: Expected failure. 2 of 3 failed: roots A01-A07 reached argv wrong (e.g. [C:" --report <file>]; two trailing backslashes lost one), and the census found the hand-quoted Invoke-HookedRun line. File restored afterwards.

Published exe with the real hook. tree\ read through read-window.ps1, then launched through Invoke-HookedRun in rows mode: exit 0, report root = 'tree\' as passed, closing rows line present, header = core.unreadable = rows = 0. Took 6 s.

W-001 run the way it will be used, with a trailing backslash on the root. Report written, 1 row (code 5 'access denied', still refused), checker controls all held, verdict held. Kernel pool paged +2.2 MB, nonpaged +1.3 MB. Took 5 s.
HookCases' by-name loader picks up Format-AppArgument, and its Start-App launches work. Took 86 s.

559 of 562 passed. The 3 failures are the known, open last-access tests (Q-190): LastAccessTests.AFolderThatRefusesWriteAttributesIsListedPlainlyAndCountedInFull and two in HeldOpenTreeTests. TEMP is C:\WINDOWS\TEMP in this shell. They are unrelated to this change.

deviations: The review asked for the doubling in Invoke-HookedRun or Start-App. I put it in one helper, Format-AppArgument, and routed all 15 hand-quoted launch sites through it, not only Invoke-HookedRun: closing the class means every producer. Start-App itself is unchanged, because the raw-argument cases (C-007, C-009, C-014) pass arrays on purpose.
C-013 now also makes a hooked rows-mode run, so it was added to $HookedCases and building the hook is part of running it.
follow_ups: eng/read-window.ps1 and tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1 each keep their own copy of the doubling rule, because they cannot load WindowCases.ps1's helper. AppArgumentTests' census pins both, but a shared helper would remove the copies.
not_built: No whole-C:\ W-001 run here. Review M8 makes that the owner's run, and the command is in docs/design/SL-089-seams.md. The argv defect that would have stopped it is what this attempt fixed.
